Indonesia is the world's largest island nation, stretching from Sumatra to New Guinea, independent since 1945. On the map it replaces the Dutch East Indies, whose borders it inherited.

Sukarno and Mohammad Hatta declared independence on 17 August 1945, two days after Japan surrendered. The Dutch tried to return, and four years of war and diplomacy followed before they handed over sovereignty in December 1949. Western New Guinea passed to Indonesia in the 1960s.

  • Sukarno ruled with growing personal power, which he called Guided Democracy.
  • In 1965 and 1966, after a failed coup blamed on the Communist Party, the army and its allies killed hundreds of thousands of suspected communists.
  • General Suharto then ruled for over thirty years. His New Order brought steady growth, oil wealth, the transmigration of people from Java to other islands, and the occupation of East Timor in 1975.
  • The Asian financial crisis brought the fall of Suharto in 1998 and a return to elections.
  • East Timor became independent in 2002, and the tsunami of 2004 struck Aceh hardest of all.

Indonesia has the largest Muslim population of any country, and hundreds of languages united by Indonesian, a form of Malay.
sum: Indonesia is the world's largest island nation, stretching from Sumatra to New Guinea, independent since 1945. On the map it replaces the Dutch East Indies, whose borders it inherited.
